# Start-ZbxPassiveProxy

## SYNOPSIS

Starts a passive proxy's listener as a session: the server pushes configuration and pulls history until stopped.

## SYNTAX

```
Start-ZbxPassiveProxy [-Name] <string> [-AllowedPeer] <string[]> [-Address <string>] [-Port <int>] -Version <Version> [-TlsAccept <ZabbixTlsAcceptModes[]>] [-PassThru] [-PskIdentity <string>] [-Psk <SecureString>] [-Certificate <string>] [-CertificateKey <string>] [-CertificateAuthority <string>] [-CertificateRevocationList <string>] [-ServerIssuer <string>] [-ServerSubject <string>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

-AllowedPeer is required: the listener accepts connections only from the peers it names. -Version is required: the server's major.minor, which it never tells a passive proxy and without which it never configures one. Write history for the server to pull with Send-ZbxPassiveProxyHistory. To take the server's connections over TLS, give the proxy's credentials (-PskIdentity and -Psk, or -Certificate, -CertificateKey and -CertificateAuthority): the listener then accepts those kinds only, unless -TlsAccept says otherwise.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Start a passive proxy's listener

```powershell
Start-ZbxPassiveProxy -Name 'dmz-proxy' -AllowedPeer '127.0.0.1' -Version '7.4' -Port 30160
Get-ZbxPassiveProxyStatus -Name 'dmz-proxy' | Select-Object Name, Started
Stop-ZbxPassiveProxy -Name 'dmz-proxy'
```

The session listens on -Port (10051 by default) for the server, which pushes the configuration and pulls history. -AllowedPeer is required: the server's addresses, CIDR blocks or DNS names; anyone else is refused. -Version is required: the server's major.minor, which a server never tells a passive proxy.

### Example 2: Listen on one interface for the server's subnet

```powershell
Start-ZbxPassiveProxy -Name 'dmz-proxy' -AllowedPeer '127.0.0.1', '10.0.0.0/24' -Version '7.4' -Address '127.0.0.1' -Port 30160
(Get-ZbxPassiveProxyStatus -Name 'dmz-proxy').Listener | Select-Object LocalEndPoint
Stop-ZbxPassiveProxy -Name 'dmz-proxy'
```

-Address binds one interface instead of every one. The server polls the proxy object's Address/Port (New-ZbxProxy -OperatingMode Passive); Send-ZbxPassiveProxyHistory then queues values for hosts it has configured.

### Example 3: Keep the listener for the length of a script

```powershell
$proxy = Start-ZbxPassiveProxy -Name 'dmz-proxy' -AllowedPeer '127.0.0.1' -Version '7.4' -Port 30160 -PassThru
try {
    'Listening as {0} since {1:u}' -f $proxy.Name, $proxy.Started
}
finally {
    Stop-ZbxPassiveProxy -Name 'dmz-proxy'
}
```

-PassThru writes the session; the finally block always frees the port, even on failure.
